title: Cleaning
description: Professional ozonation for cleaning companies: removal of ingrained odors, post-fire treatment, pet odor removal, vehicle ozonation and deep cleaning of carpets and upholstery.

carpet-cleaning.title: Carpets and upholstery
carpet-cleaning.content:
Carpets and upholstery are the main odor reservoirs in a room. Textile fibers absorb dust, fungal spores, bacteria, skin particles, sweat and spills. Over time a characteristic musty odor forms that normal cleaning cannot remove.

Ozonation complements conventional dry cleaning with deep deodorization and disinfection. After wet carpet cleaning, ozone penetrates fibers and destroys remaining bacteria, fungal spores and odor molecules.

For local treatment of furniture or carpet, "chamber ozonation" is used: the item is covered with plastic film and ozone is fed underneath. Exposure: 2–4 hours. This creates high ozone concentration directly in the item.

Ozonation is effective after flooding: it removes damp odor and prevents mold in wet furniture and carpets. Treatment should be done after items are dried.

intro.paragraph1: Carpets and upholstery are the main dirt reservoirs in a room. Textile fibers absorb dust, fungal spores, bacteria, skin particles, sweat and spills. Over time a characteristic musty odor forms that vacuuming or even dry cleaning cannot remove.
intro.paragraph2: Dry cleaning removes dirt and stains but does not always handle deep odors and microorganisms in the material. Ozonation is the ideal complement, providing full deodorization and disinfection after wet cleaning.

highlight1.title: Why carpets smell:
highlight1.text: Up to 100,000 dust mites live in one gram of carpet dust. Their droppings are a strong allergen. Bacteria break down organic matter and release odorous compounds. Ozone destroys both mites and bacteria, eliminating the cause of odor.

items.title: What is treated with ozone
items: Carpets and carpeting — floor, wall, hand-made
Upholstered furniture — sofas, armchairs, poufs, benches
Mattresses and pillows — including orthopedic
Curtains and drapes — without removing from the rail
Soft toys — safe for children's items
Car seats — as a separate service

methods.title: Textile ozonation methods
methods.paragraph: There are two main methods: whole-room treatment and local chamber treatment of a specific item.

steps.title: Item preparation
steps.description: If needed, do preliminary dry cleaning or vacuuming. Allow to dry completely. Lightly mist the surface with a sprayer to activate soiling.

steps.title: Creating the chamber
steps.description: Cover the item with plastic film. Seal the edges to the floor to form an airtight "chamber". Leave a small opening for the ozone generator hose.

steps.title: Connecting the generator
steps.description: Insert the hose under the film. Secure so ozone does not escape. Turn on the generator. The film should inflate slightly from the gas flow.

steps.title: Exposure
steps.description: Hold for 2-4 hours depending on odor intensity. For heavy soiling — up to 8 hours. You can turn pillows periodically for even treatment.

steps.title: Finishing
steps.description: Turn off the generator. Remove the film. Ventilate the item for 30-60 minutes. Ozone fully decays, leaving no trace.

highlight.title: Tip:
highlight.text: To boost effect on furniture or carpet with urine stains, pretreat soiled areas with an enzymatic cleaner. Then dry and run ozonation.

afterCleaning.title: Ozonation after dry cleaning
afterCleaning.paragraph: Ozonation is the ideal final step of professional dry cleaning:
items: Removes odor of chemicals used in cleaning
Kills bacteria that may remain after wet treatment
Eliminates deep odors that dry cleaning did not remove
Prevents mold in damp spots
Deactivates allergens (mites, spores, pollen)
Increases perceived value of the dry cleaning service
tableRows: Removal of dust, hair, large debris

afterFlood.title: Ozonation after flooding
afterFlood.paragraph: Flooding is a special case requiring quick action. Wet textiles are an ideal environment for mold. Ozonation prevents it:
items: First dry carpets and furniture as much as possible (dehumidifiers, fans)
Residual moisture should not exceed 15-20%
Run ozonation at the first signs of musty odor
Ozone concentration: 40-60 mg/m³ for mold prevention
Treatment time: 6-12 hours for full disinfection
If mold is found — treat with inhibitor before ozonation

highlight.title: Important:
highlight.text: If mold is already visible on the surface, ozonation alone is not enough. First remove mold mechanically and treat with antiseptic. Ozone will destroy remaining spores and odor but will not remove the mycelium physically.

materials.title: Safety for materials
materials.paragraph: Ozone is safe for most textile materials when recommended concentrations are followed:
items: Natural fabrics (cotton, linen, wool) — safe
Synthetic fabrics (polyester, nylon) — safe
Natural leather — safe, but conditioning afterward is recommended
Latex and rubber — long treatment at high concentrations not recommended
Dyed fabrics — safe, ozone does not bleach at recommended settings
Delicate fabrics (silk, viscose) — safe at standard concentrations

highlight.title: Note:
highlight.text: Ozone may slightly accelerate aging of rubber and latex with repeated high-concentration treatments. For furniture with rubber elements use standard modes.
